tests: The results below were produced on November 25, 2026, on the candidate before launch (commit a21cc9e, the commit that was merged). Live verification results are in the launch record above.
Production test suite: all 3,293 checks pass in launch mode, with all five articles published, and CI is green.
Interactions on the final build: 134 scripted checks pass in Chromium and Firefox.
Accessibility: axe-core (WCAG 2.1 A and AA, plus best practices) reports no issues on any of the 21 pages at 375 and 1440 pixels.

Responsive: Chromium and Firefox at 320, 375, 390, 768, 1024 and 1440 pixels on all 21 pages. No horizontal overflow, console errors, broken images, missing alt text, text under 12 pixels, or touch targets under 24 pixels.
Layout shift on a fresh load: 0 on every page, desktop and phone.

Interactions: 134 scripted checks pass in Chromium and Firefox: keyboard order and focus, menus and Escape, the presence map by click, touch and keyboard, the Pause control, the diagnostic, the five layers, the Digital Presence Check (including that it stores and sends nothing), the Insights library, the article contents list, reduced motion, and no JavaScript.

Contact form: on staging it is disabled and sends nothing. On the candidate source, validation, the ?need= prefill, the honeypot, the mailto fallback and the Web3Forms request were verified with the request intercepted, so nothing was sent.
URLs: all five legacy .html stubs redirect to their directory URLs, services.html#seo lands on the SEO card, canonicals match the sitemap, and no existing URL changed.

Structured data: every block parses, the shared Person record is byte-identical to the live copy on all three pages, and the Organization record is identical wherever it is described, including on the June press release page.
Articles: unchanged in this round. Every quotation was checked against its source earlier on November 25, 2026.
Third parties: a page view on the candidate makes no third-party request.
Links: every internal link resolves, and external links answer apart from two sites that refuse automated requests (LinkedIn, and ProjectManagement.com, which was confirmed in a real browser).
KenAshe.ai pull requests: the Vercel preview build is the build check. The Digest pipeline's own tests give the same result before and after the prompt change.

perfNote: Laboratory measurements, not Lighthouse scores and not field data. Measured on the published staging copy on November 24, 2026, in Chromium through the DevTools Protocol; the changes made on November 25 were to text and metadata only. Each figure is the median of three cold loads. Phone figures use a 412 by 823 viewport with 150 ms latency, 1.6 Mbps down and the processor slowed four times, close to Lighthouse's mobile preset. Transfer and requests are for a first visit on desktop, with nothing cached, and include one staging-only script. No page made a third-party request.
